answer: At each tide turn, every identity files a fresh profile of its one assigned dune segment, measured in the same 90-second window. Assignment locks 150 units for 12 epochs. Verifiers compare each filing against two neighbour filings and the tide gauge: a copied, late, or inconsistent profile earns zero and forfeits 10 units. A quill nib registered to the segment signs each filing, and its wear trace is checked against earlier filings, so one nib cannot sign for two segments in one window. One honest agent locks 150 once; 1,000 fakes lock 150,000 and need 1,000 live sensors filing simultaneously.
